population.joinMultiplicity.rationale: income_trees contains 4 duplicated ZIPs (10463, 11205, 11218, 11370), each appearing twice with identical Estimate_Median_income and Estimate_Mean_income. These are lookup duplication; joining raw would double those ZIPs' trees (Queens 256056 vs 252846) and double-weight their income (79312.57 vs 79366.74). fields.rationale: The combined dataset unifies the trees data with the income data by ZIP code, with trees as the base (690,626 tree records); each combined row is a tree carrying its ZIP's income. 'the average mean income for each of these three boroughs' therefore averages the per-record mean income over the borough's qualifying tree records (tree-weighted). The rejected alternative (ZIP-unweighted = each ZIP counted equally) would ignore that ZIPs hold very different numbers of trees, which the 'combined dataset' wording does not call for. Advisor tool was unavailable (HTTP 451); decided on the literal reading and disclosed.
